cells.tense: Right now you register what counts before you can explain how you know it.
cells.ask: Say your read on one thing out loud before you can back it up, and let the other person take it or leave it.
cells.core:
You catch what counts before you can explain how you know. A name, a hesitation, a detail — it arrives first and the reasons catch up later. Not needing the reasons first is why people bring you the real question instead of the polite one. What you see tends to hold up, and you've stopped bracing against that.

Under weight you keep your shape and stay open, and the two are working together. What this can feed next is structure: a plain way to keep what you notice usable. Say one reading out loud while it's fresh. Even to one person, that gives it somewhere to live.

cells.tense: You are bracing for the point where the whole picture has to be known, so you gather instead of moving.
cells.ask: Take the version you already have and act on it today, before the next piece arrives.
cells.core:
One detail tells you what a whole situation is, and you often move on it well before you could prove it. The trouble is you've started waiting for the moment no proof is needed. Gathering, checking, keeping the decision open until the picture fills in. Collecting feels like the work, then it becomes the thing keeping you from the work.

The read you'd need is already here. One thing you've been circling is already clear enough to act on. Let it be enough, put it to use, and let the rest arrive afterward. The finish line you keep waiting for is one you're drawing yourself.

cells.tense: A while back you stopped acting on what you noticed, and that is where you are.
cells.ask: Write down one thing you noticed before anyone said it. Leave it somewhere you'll see it tomorrow.
cells.core:
You can feel it when a read is right — the body knows before the head does, and when you trust that, you move cleanly. Lately you notice first and then wait. The read goes out for a second opinion, or you hold it until someone else says it so it counts. What you see has gone quiet in you.

Insight isn't the shortage — trust in your own perception is, small and specific. It comes back one moment at a time, not by force. Write one down today, before the doubting gets to it.

cells.tense: You are deciding things on a knowing you haven't claimed, then calling the decisions random.
cells.ask: Catch one choice you made today that you called luck, and say out loud that it was yours.
cells.core:
You can read a situation and act on it, and most days that works well enough that you don't think about it. What happens now is quieter: the read fires, you decide, and the story afterward is that it just came to you. A person gets picked, a path gets dropped, a room gets left. The perceiving ran the whole time; only the credit went missing.

Small cost, paid over and over — each time you hand the choice to luck, you hand off a little of what's yours. Owning one call you already made is enough to start.
